steps.what: Read systems and network configurations
Draft changes to improve configurations

loop.input: configuration rows and the recommendation template
loop.output: a draft that cites configuration ids
loop.check: Every cited configuration id is on the export
loop.stop: One pass, then drop any sentence with no configuration id
loop.why_not_simpler: Whether a change is worth the cost is not a fixed lookup

steps.what: Determine hardware or software requirements
Recommend changes related to those requirements
Comment on the recommended configuration changes

tasks.design: Current configurations sit on a {BI} view. A bounded note in {DOCS} drafts changes that would improve them, citing only configuration ids. The systems administrator determines hardware or software requirements and signs the recommendation. Applying the change is a later task. The draft does not touch a live system.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requirements were rewritten from old documents, so a reader could not see which configuration a recommendation relied on.
tasks.enabler_now: A configuration export can carry an id, a system id and an owner that a recommendation can cite.
tasks.still_hard: Whether a change is worth the cost and the risk is a business call, not a template.
tasks.human_edge: The administrator recommends the changes and sets the hardware or software requirements.

ambition.what: Refresh configuration recommendations every quarter, not only at the yearly budget

tasks.altitude: Less time collecting configuration facts. The administrator can refuse a recommendation that cites no configuration.

reach.task: Comment on the recommended changes before a design
reach.learn: Which requirements are signed and which configurations were left out

evidence.claim: A recommendation of this kind is a judgement written down. Gathering the configurations is the part that repeats. Choosing the change does not.
Digest [S16] and [S18] say that for firms in scope, the Dutch cyber duty of care includes patching and supply-chain measures. A recommendation may name those. Scope depends on sector and size.
Digest [S28] reports a coding agent that deleted a production database despite instructions, so this draft must not change live configurations by itself.

assumptions: Focal role is the systems administrator. The task ends at a signed recommendation and the requirements. Implementing the change is a later task.
Input contract: configuration id, system id, owner, requirement type, cost note. Producer of the export is the console. Rows with no configuration id are left out of the draft.
Native reports are configured before custom code. The draft is not connected to a console write. The meeting prior fits the decision, not the gathering.
unknowns: Who funds a requirement the administrator recommends.
Whether this firm is in scope of the cyber duty of care.
research_questions: What share of recommendations from last year was never decided?
How often does a requirement cite a configuration that no longer exists?

already_counted.description: Administrator edits the changes draft before determining requirements
Determining requirements stays with the administrator

incremental.description: Update the recommendation template when a new requirement type appears

approvals.approved_version: recommendation version signed in this review

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes configuration exports are incomplete, so the draft is thin and the recommendation is written by hand. The high case assumes a clean draft, while determining requirements and signing the recommendation stay manual. No live change is counted as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Facilitate the purchases list from the need

loop.input: request mail and the purchase form
loop.output: a list that copies system id and quantity
loop.check: Each row has a system id and a quantity that appear in the mail
loop.stop: If quantity is missing, leave the row blank and stop that mail
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text needs do not map to a quantity by a fixed table

steps.what: Quote purchases the vendors were asked
Confirm purchases with company personnel
Coordinate and sign the requested purchases
File the signed purchases request

tasks.design: A {WORKFLOW} form holds the purchases list: system id, quantity and owner. A bounded note drafts it from the request mail. The vendor engineer quotes. The network architect confirms the need for company personnel. The systems administrator coordinates and signs. The signed request is filed to {PROCUREMENT}. The talks stay conversations.
tasks.previous_blocker: Purchase requests were mail threads with no system id, so a quote could not be matched to a need and the same ask was repeated.
tasks.enabler_now: A request can carry a system id, a quantity and an owner that a quote and a signature can both cite.
tasks.still_hard: A vendor's price and a colleague's priority are conversations. A form does not settle them.
tasks.human_edge: The administrator coordinates the purchases and signs only the request people and the vendor have both addressed.
tasks.altitude: The list and the filing shrink. The administrator still coordinates the talks and can refuse a purchase.

reach.task: Quote the purchases they were asked for
reach.learn: Which purchases are signed and which still have no quantity

evidence.claim: Coordinating a purchase is mostly mail and calls. The list and the filing are the parts that can be a form. The talks cannot.

Digest [S16] and [S18] say that for firms in scope, the Dutch cyber duty of care includes supply-chain measures. A signed purchase list can name the supplier. Scope depends on sector and size, and this task does not decide it.

assumptions: Focal role is the systems administrator. The task ends when a signed purchases request is filed. Paying the invoice is out of scope. Vendor and personnel time is not the administrator's time.

Input contract: request id, system id, quantity, owner, supplier name. Producer of the need is company personnel via the network architect or the system user. A request with no quantity is not signed.

Native procurement fields are configured before custom code. Conversations with vendors and personnel stay person to person. The workflow prior overstates what a job can do: the shape is a form, not the talk.
unknowns: Who has authority to commit spend.
Whether a preferred supplier list exists.
Whether this firm is in scope of supply-chain duties.
research_questions: What share of purchases is requested twice?
How long does a quote usually take to come back?

already_counted.description: Administrator checks the purchases list before the talks
Coordination and signature stay with the administrator

incremental.description: Update purchase fields when a new supplier type is added
Vendors resend quotes that omitted a system id

approvals.approved_version: purchases version signed in this review

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes requests stay as mail, so the list is retyped and the talks are unchanged. The high case assumes the list and the filing run from fields, while coordinating vendors and personnel stays manual. Vendor time is not counted as the administrator's saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: State customer needs for the system
Gather information pertaining to customer needs

loop.output: rows that copy need id and system id
loop.check: Each row cites a need id the user stated
loop.stop: If the need has no system id, leave the row blank and stop
loop.why_not_simpler: Meeting prose does not map to a system id by a fixed table

steps.what: Identify and evaluate system requirements
Interpret and predict network requirements
Sign the system requirements version

tasks.design: System users state customer needs in a meeting and on a {WORKFLOW} form. A bounded note gathers the information that pertains to those needs. The systems administrator identifies, evaluates, interprets and predicts system and network requirements, then signs one version in {DOCS}. The meeting stays a conversation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Needs lived in meeting notes with no system id, so two readers produced two requirements lists.
tasks.enabler_now: A form can hold a need id, a system id and a user, so a requirements note can cite the need instead of the prose.
tasks.still_hard: Predicting what people will need next is a judgement, and a user may not know the constraint.
tasks.human_edge: The administrator evaluates the requirements and can refuse a need the form does not support.

ambition.what: Small-site users can submit a need without waiting for the quarterly visit

tasks.altitude: Notes are shorter to assemble. The meeting and the evaluation stay with the administrator.

reach.task: Confirm the needs they stated were heard
reach.learn: Which requirements are signed and which needs are still open

evidence.claim: Gathering needs is a conversation plus a write-up. The conversation does not become a record by itself. The write-up can cite fields.
In a mid-size firm the customer of this task is usually an internal system user, not an outside buyer. Treating them as outside customers would overstate the task.

assumptions: Focal role is the systems administrator. The task ends at a signed requirements version. Building the change is a later task. The customer here is the system user.
Input contract: need id, system id, user, stated need, date. Producer is the system user. If the form is empty the administrator types the same fields from the meeting and marks them manual.
The meeting stays person to person. Native forms are configured before custom code. A draft requirement is not treated as signed.
unknowns: Whether some needs come from outside customers rather than staff.
Who accepts a requirement the user dislikes.
Which systems have no owner to attach a need to.
research_questions: What share of needs has no system id?
How often does the signed requirement differ from the user's first statement?

already_counted.description: Administrator checks gathered needs before evaluating them

incremental.description: Update the needs form when a new system type appears

approvals.approved_version: requirements version signed in this review

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes needs stay as meeting prose, so the gather step saves little and evaluation is unchanged. The high case assumes a form, while the meeting and the evaluation stay manual. Building the system is not counted as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Judge repair or replacement from records

steps.what: Open equipment performance records
Analyze performance records for this asset

loop.input: performance rows and repair history for one asset id
loop.output: a note that cites the asset id and the repair ids
loop.check: Every cited repair id belongs to that asset id
loop.stop: If the asset id is missing, return an empty note and stop
loop.why_not_simpler: An intermittent fault does not match a fixed threshold

steps.what: Determine the need for repair or replacement
Advise on replacement lead time
File the signed repair or replacement decision

tasks.design: Equipment performance records open on a {BI} view with an asset id. A bounded note analyzes those records against the repair history. The systems administrator determines whether repair or replacement is needed and signs that decision. The vendor engineer may state a lead time. The note does not replace the equipment.
tasks.previous_blocker: Performance records and repair history lived in different sheets, so the case for replacement was reassembled each time.
tasks.enabler_now: An asset id can join the performance export to the repair record.
tasks.still_hard: An intermittent fault does not cross a simple threshold, and replacing the wrong asset is costly.
tasks.human_edge: The administrator determines the need for repair or replacement and can wait when the records are thin.

ambition.what: Review equipment that is near replacement every month, not only after a failure

tasks.altitude: Less time joining records. The repair or replacement decision stays with the administrator.

reach.task: Advise on replacement lead time for a signed asset
reach.learn: Which assets are signed for replacement and which are still repair

evidence.claim: Deciding repair or replacement is a judgement on records. Joining the records is the part that repeats. The decision does not.
Digest [S7] and [S8] describe a managed detection service that speeds investigation for mid-size firms, while a person still decides what to do.
Digest [S13] reports an observational study of live security operations with shorter resolve times after a generative assistant versus matched peers. It was not a randomised trial.
Digest [S28] reports a coding agent that deleted a production database despite instructions, so an analysis must not replace or alter live equipment by itself.

assumptions: Focal role is the systems administrator. The task ends at a signed repair or replacement decision. Doing the repair is a later task.
Input contract: asset id, metric, period, last repair id, site. Producer is the performance export joined to the repair record. An asset with no id stays off the note.
Native performance views are configured before custom code. The modest meeting prior fits: this task is screens and records, not a workshop.
unknowns: Which assets have no performance export.
What age counts as due for replacement in this firm.
research_questions: What share of assets has performance records but no repair history?
How often is the first replacement decision reversed?

already_counted.description: Administrator reviews a thin performance analysis
The repair or replacement decision stays

incremental.description: Add an asset id when new equipment is installed
Vendor time on lead times beyond the first reply

approvals.approved_version: repair or replacement decision signed for this asset id
the same signed repair or replacement decision

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes asset ids do not join, so the analysis stays manual. The high case assumes a clean note, while the repair or replacement decision stays manual. Doing the repair is not counted as saved, and nothing changes the equipment unattended.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The administrator spends less time assembling records, and keeps recommendation, purchase and replacement decisions.
reach: The network architect receives a signed recommendation instead of a slide of unmarked configurations.
The vendor engineer receives a purchase list that already names the system and the quantity.
skills_to_grow: Write a recommendation as requirements with a system id, not a prose wish.
Keep a vendor conversation as a conversation and file only the signed purchase.
Separate an equipment record that shows a fault from the decision to repair or replace.
role.ambitious_version: Recommendations, purchase requests and repair decisions each carry a signed version, and none of them changes a live system by itself.
